legalName: Motion to Dismiss the Charges and Application to Expunge After a First-Offence DUI Deferral, W. Va. Code § 17C-5-2b(c) and (g)
publicName: Clear a first DUI that was deferred and dismissed after the test and lock program
mechanism: Read at source on 2026-08-06, § 17C-5-2b operates on a person who pleads to or is found guilty of the offence defined in § 17C-5-2(e), has no prior DUI-type conviction, and notifies the court within 30 days of arrest of the intention to participate in a deferral. On those conditions the court, without entering a judgment of guilt, shall defer further proceedings and place the person on probation conditioned on successful completion of the Motor Vehicle Alcohol Test and Lock Program under § 17C-5A-3a, for at least 165 days after a 15-day licence suspension and completed within one year thereafter. The section then creates two separate participant-facing submissions. First, under subsection (c), when the defendant has satisfactorily completed the programme and complied with its conditions, the defendant may move the court for an order dismissing the charges; that motion must be supported by the defendant's affidavit and by certification of the Division of Motor Vehicles that the programme was successfully completed, and the prosecuting attorney has 30 days after service to advise the judge of objections, in the absence of which the court shall dismiss. Second, under subsection (g), after a period of not less than one year beginning to run immediately on the expiration of the term of probation, the person may apply to the court for an order expunging all official records of the arrest, trial and conviction, except those maintained by the Division of Motor Vehicles, provided that a person previously convicted of a felony may not make that motion; objections are filed within 30 days of service, and if objections are filed the court holds a hearing and, if it determines there was no serious or repeated violation of the conditions of probation, it shall order the expungement. Only one discharge and dismissal is available under the section, and § 61-11-25(a) independently provides that no Division of Motor Vehicles record may be expunged by virtue of any order entered pursuant to § 17C-5-2b.

rationale: The registry declares outputStrategyDeclared 'composed' with compositionMode 'sequential': unit 1 must have produced a dismissal and discharge before unit 2 becomes available at all, and a further year must run from the expiration of probation before unit 2 can be made.

Both registry units declare outputStrategy 'custom_pleading', outputStrategyStatus 'resolved', packetIdentity 'identified' and available true. The unit descriptions state in terms that no West Virginia Judiciary form exists for either: "the Court Forms index was read at source on 2026-08-06 and publishes exactly five expungement forms, none for this section."

The registry packetSet lists seven required components. Five carry outputStrategy 'custom_pleading' (primary filing, supporting affidavit, secondary filing, supporting timeline, certificate of service) and are expressed as pleading_document units. Two carry outputStrategy 'process_guidance' (records checklist, filing instructions) and are expressed as participant_instruction units.

No official_form_dependency unit exists. Every West Virginia expungement form catalogued in the committed state pack and named in the compiled profile — SCA-C900, SCA-C903, SCA-C906, SCA-C907, SCA-C912 — is a § 61-11-25 or § 61-11-26 instrument. None has a § 17C-5-2b role.

No agency_request_letter unit exists. The Division of Motor Vehicles certification the subsection (c) motion must be supported by is recorded as obtained by asking, with no form number and no letter named.
No cover_sheet unit exists. The registry packetSet has seven components and none is a cover sheet.

authoritySpine.description: The offence the deferral operates on. Section 17C-5-2b applies to a person who pleads to or is found guilty of the offence defined in § 17C-5-2(e) and has no prior DUI-type conviction.

The deferral itself: on notice to the court within 30 days of arrest of the intention to participate, the court, without entering a judgment of guilt, shall defer further proceedings and place the person on probation. The 30-day notice window is charge-stage criminal defence and is expressly outside the adopted product scope; this route serves only the person for whom a deferral was already granted.
Probation conditioned on successful completion of the Motor Vehicle Alcohol Test and Lock Program, for at least 165 days after a 15-day licence suspension and completed within one year thereafter.

The Motor Vehicle Alcohol Test and Lock Program the probation is conditioned on. The Division of Motor Vehicles certifies successful completion, and that certification is what the subsection (c) motion must be supported by.

Unit 1. When the defendant has satisfactorily completed the programme and complied with its conditions, the defendant may move the court for an order dismissing the charges; the motion must be supported by the defendant's affidavit and by certification of the Division of Motor Vehicles that the programme was successfully completed; the prosecuting attorney has 30 days after service to advise the judge of objections, in the absence of which the court shall dismiss.
The legal effect of the unit 1 disposition: dismissal and discharge without adjudication of guilt, which is not a conviction for the purpose of disqualifications or disabilities.
Only one discharge and dismissal is available under the section. A participant who has already had one is excluded.

The four ineligibility categories: any prosecution in which any violation of any other provision of article 17C-5 has been charged (f)(1); a commercial driver's licence holder or operator of commercial motor vehicles (f)(2); a person previously having had a licence revoked for a same-elements offence under a municipal ordinance of this state or any other state or a statute of the United States or any other state (f)(3); and a person as to whom a court entered an order finding a refusal of the secondary chemical test under § 17C-5-7a (f)(4).

Unit 2. After a period of not less than one year beginning to run immediately on the expiration of the term of probation, the person may apply to the court for an order expunging all official records of the arrest, trial and conviction, except those maintained by the Division of Motor Vehicles; a person previously convicted of a felony may not make that motion; objections are filed within 30 days of service, and if objections are filed the court holds a hearing and, if it determines there was no serious or repeated violation of the conditions of probation, it shall order the expungement.

A person whose case is disposed of under the section must pay the court costs that could be assessed against a person convicted of the offence; payment may have been made a condition of probation. No amount is stated in any source read for this track.

Carried in the track authority list. The disclosure protection the registry records for this section is that a person as to whom dismissal and discharge have been effected is not guilty of perjury, false swearing or otherwise giving a false statement by reason of failing to disclose the arrest or trial, except in response to an inquiry made in connection with a subsequent offence under § 17C-5-2.
The independent hard limit: no Division of Motor Vehicles record may be expunged by virtue of any order entered pursuant to § 17C-5-2b. The criminal record can be cleared; the driving record cannot.

Section 61-11-26b bars expunging DUI convictions; § 61-11-26(o) imposes a once-per-lifetime limit; the § 61-11-26 fee regime is a civil filing fee plus a $100 State Police processing fee. units.legalUnit: Section 17C-5-2b(c) motion to dismiss the charges after satisfactory completion of the Motor Vehicle Alcohol Test and Lock Program

applicability.includedWhen: Screening reports all of: the court deferred the proceedings and placed the participant on probation under § 17C-5-2b (deferralOrderDate answered); the participant successfully completed the Motor Vehicle Alcohol Test and Lock Program and complied with its conditions (programCompletionDate answered); and stageNeeded reports that the charges have NOT yet been dismissed.
applicability.excludedWhen: Screening reports any of: stageNeeded reports the charges were already dismissed (that participant goes to unit 3, not here); the participant did not complete or was removed from the test and lock program; otherArticleCharges reports another offence under article 17C-5 was charged in the same prosecution; commercialLicence reports a commercial driver's licence or commercial vehicle operation at the time of the offence; priorLicenceRevocation reports an earlier revocation for a same-elements offence in any jurisdiction; secondaryTestRefusal reports a court order finding refusal of the secondary chemical test; priorDeferral reports an earlier discharge and dismissal under this section; or the charge is still live and no deferral has been granted.

units.notes: Drafted as a controlled pleading because no West Virginia Judiciary form exists for a § 17C-5-2b filing and the subsection supplies the destination, the operative facts and the relief. The words expunge, expunged and expungement are prohibited in this component's document text: this stage produces dismissal and discharge, not expungement, and merging the two is the error the registry models the units apart to prevent. A prior felony conviction does NOT exclude this unit — the felony bar sits in subsection (g).

units.legalUnit: The defendant's affidavit that § 17C-5-2b(c) requires the motion to dismiss to be supported by

applicability.includedWhen: Always with unit 1. Subsection (c) requires the motion to be supported by the defendant's affidavit, so the affidavit is produced whenever the motion is.
applicability.excludedWhen: Whenever unit 1 is excluded. It is never produced on its own and never with the subsection (g) application, for which no source records an affidavit.

units.notes: The one notarised document in the route. The registry records notarization as "Required on the unit 1 supporting affidavit" and lists the affidavit signature, date and jurat as a manual completion item. No source read for this track prescribes the jurat wording or the class of officer, so none is invented; the component renders a signature and jurat area and leaves the wording to be confirmed. Every averment is the participant's own statement of fact; none is generated or supplemented.

units.legalUnit: Section 17C-5-2b(g) application to expunge all official records of the arrest, trial and conviction, except those maintained by the Division of Motor Vehicles

applicability.includedWhen: Screening reports all of: the proceedings were deferred and probation imposed under § 17C-5-2b; the charges were dismissed and the participant discharged (stageNeeded reports the dismissal already happened, dismissalDate answered); the participant's answer to probationExpiryDate is at least one year in the past, measured from the expiration of probation and NOT from the dismissal; priorFelonyConviction reports no felony conviction anywhere; and probationViolations reports that nobody has alleged a breach of the conditions of probation.
applicability.excludedWhen: Screening reports any of: no dismissal and discharge has been entered (stageNeeded reports the charges are not yet dismissed — that participant goes to unit 1); less than one year has run since probation expired; probationExpiryDate is unanswered or answered only from memory with no written confirmation; priorFelonyConviction reports any felony conviction in West Virginia or anywhere else, which bars this motion outright under (g)(1); probationViolations reports an allegation of a serious or repeated violation; any subsection (f) bar applies; or the participant's stated goal is the driving record, which this order never reaches.

units.notes: Cannot be reached until unit 1 has produced a dismissal and discharge and a further year has run from the expiration of the probation term. The requested relief is stated in the subsection's own terms, including its own exception for Division of Motor Vehicles records, so the application can never be read as asking for the driving record. The notice line carries a hearing date that is left blank: a hearing happens only if objections are filed, and the court sets the date.

counselFlags.statement: No West Virginia Judiciary form exists for either the § 17C-5-2b(c) motion to dismiss or the § 17C-5-2b(g) application to expunge. The Court Forms index was read at source on 2026-08-06 and publishes exactly five expungement forms — SCA-C900, SCA-C903, SCA-C906, SCA-C907 and SCA-C912 — none of which is a § 17C-5-2b filing; the committed state pack catalogues the same five and ties each to § 61-11-25 or § 61-11-26. On that basis the controlling review's build blocker is answered in the negative and every court document in this route is a custom pleading. Whether an unpublished local form is used in some courts was not tested.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: Whether any court uses an unpublished local form for a § 17C-5-2b filing.

counselFlags.statement: Whether unit 1 is reachable in practice by a self-represented participant whose deferral was granted years earlier and whose charges were never formally dismissed is not established. Section 17C-5-2b(c) was read in full at source on 2026-08-06 and places no time limit on the motion to dismiss, but the section assumes a live case file and a defendant still before the court. Where the file has been closed administratively, whether the motion is still the right vehicle is unknown. Nothing in this route asserts that it is.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: Where a participant completed the test and lock program years ago but no order of dismissal was ever entered, is the § 17C-5-2b(c) motion to dismiss still the correct vehicle, and does LegalEase generate it, or does a stale file require counsel?

counselFlags.statement: Whether relief under § 17C-5-2b counts against the once-per-lifetime limit in § 61-11-26(o) is unsettled. Section 61-11-26(o) reaches only §§ 61-11-26 and 61-11-26a on its face, and § 17C-5-2b was read in full at source on 2026-08-06 and contains no cross-reference to it. The textual reading is that they are separate limits in separate statutes, but a participant deciding whether to spend their one lifetime conviction petition needs a settled answer. No participant copy in this route tells the participant either way.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: Whether relief under § 17C-5-2b counts against the § 61-11-26(o) once-per-lifetime limit.

counselFlags.statement: The compiled WV profile never mentions § 17C-5-2b, the Motor Vehicle Alcohol Test and Lock Program or § 17C-5A-3a, and none of its seven pathways is this one. Worse for routing, the committed state pack states flatly that "DUI convictions cannot be expunged" and that DUI under § 17C-5-2 is excluded from pretrial diversion. Both statements are true of the routes they describe — § 61-11-26b bars expunging DUI convictions and § 61-11-22 excludes DUI from pretrial diversion — and both would turn away exactly the participant this track exists for, whose proceedings were deferred under § 17C-5-2b without any judgment of guilt being entered. Every legal proposition in this route comes from the pinned registry entry.

counselFlags.statement: The instruments on this route are a motion (subsection (c): "the defendant may move the court") and an application (subsection (g): "the person may apply to the court"), and the registry names them exactly that. Every West Virginia Judiciary expungement form is a petition or motion under § 61-11-25 or § 61-11-26 — a different statute, with a different fee regime, a different service list, a once-per-lifetime limit, and an express bar on expunging DUI convictions. The words petition and petitioner are therefore prohibited in this route's rendered document text so the product can never read as a § 61-11-26 packet.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: The label a West Virginia court expects on each submission, and whether 'Applicant' is acceptable on the subsection (g) application.

counselFlags.statement: Service on the prosecuting attorney is what starts the 30-day objection window on both submissions, and it is the participant's own act. The registry lists the prosecuting attorney's street address and the certificate-of-service date and signature as manual completion items, to be completed by the participant from the current published address, because the certificate attests to what the participant actually did. No prosecutor name, no prosecutor address, no service date and no prosecutor position is ever prefilled, and no drafted document asserts that service was completed or that the prosecuting attorney did or did not object.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: The manner of service a West Virginia court accepts for each submission, and the form of the certificate.

counselFlags.statement: The notice line on the subsection (g) application carries a hearing date, and the registry lists it as a manual completion item because "a hearing is held only if objections are filed, and the court sets the date." It is left blank. Nothing in this route asserts that a hearing will or will not be held, states a hearing date, or predicts an outcome.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: Whether the application should carry a notice line at all where no objection has yet been filed, and what a West Virginia court expects on it.

counselFlags.statement: The two stages must never be merged into one filing. The registry models them as separate units because the required contents, the timing and the legal effect all differ: the subsection (c) motion needs the defendant's affidavit and the Division of Motor Vehicles certification and produces dismissal and discharge without adjudication of guilt; the subsection (g) application cannot be made until a further year has run from the expiration of probation, is barred outright by any prior felony conviction, and produces expungement of the criminal record. Unit 1 must have produced a dismissal before unit 2 becomes available at all. The words expunge, expunged and expungement are prohibited in the unit-1 document text for exactly this reason.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That the pipeline cannot emit the subsection (g) application at the same time as the subsection (c) motion, and that stageNeeded gates which components are produced.

counselFlags.statement: Approved for implementation stage 2 only. Section 17C-5-2b requires notice to the court within 30 days of arrest of the intention to participate in a deferral; that window is charge-stage criminal defence, is expressly outside the adopted product scope, and closes quickly. Nothing in this route may be produced for a participant whose charge is live and who has not yet given that notice — that participant needs a lawyer immediately. The route serves only the person who already completed the test and lock program.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That screening routes a live, pre-notice DUI charge to counsel and never into this route.

counselFlags.statement: Subsection (f) makes four categories ineligible for dismissal and discharge under the section: any prosecution in which any violation of any other provision of article 17C-5 has been charged; any person holding a commercial driver's licence or operating commercial motor vehicles; any person previously having had a licence revoked for an offence with the same elements under a municipal ordinance of this state or any other state or a statute of the United States or any other state; and any person as to whom a court entered an order finding a refusal of the secondary chemical test under § 17C-5-7a. Subsection (e) allows only one discharge and dismissal under the section. Each is screened as a hard exclusion and each is a self-help stop condition; none is asserted as satisfied in any drafted document.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That each subsection (f) bar and the one-discharge limit are screened before any document is produced.

counselFlags.statement: What LegalEase cannot complete: the Division of Motor Vehicles certification that the test and lock program was successfully completed. Section 17C-5-2b(c) requires the motion to dismiss to be supported by it, so the motion cannot go in without it, but it is an agency document the participant obtains by asking the Division of Motor Vehicles. No form number, no request letter and no template is recorded for it anywhere in the sources, so none is drafted and no agency_request_letter unit exists in this route. LegalEase does not obtain, receive or inspect it, and no drafted document characterises what it says.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That no pipeline stage produces or files the motion to dismiss without the participant holding the Division of Motor Vehicles certification.

counselFlags.statement: What LegalEase cannot complete: the court's finding on probation violations. If objections are filed within 30 days of service of the § 17C-5-2b(g) application, the court holds a hearing affording all parties an opportunity to be heard on whether there was any serious or repeated violation of the conditions of probation, and automated assistance ends there. Anyone alleging such a violation, and any objection that produces a hearing, is a self-help stop condition. Nothing in this route predicts an objection, a hearing, or how the court will find.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That an objection or an alleged probation violation ends automated assistance rather than producing further documents.

counselFlags.statement: Hard limit that must be disclosed: no Division of Motor Vehicles record may be expunged by virtue of an order entered pursuant to this section. Subsection (g)(1) itself excepts records maintained by the Division of Motor Vehicles, and § 61-11-25(a) says so independently. The criminal record can be cleared; the driving record cannot. A participant who is chiefly concerned about the driving record is a self-help stop condition, because this route never clears it.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That the driving-record limit is disclosed before any document is produced, and that a driving-record-motivated participant is routed out.

counselFlags.statement: The one-year window in § 17C-5-2b(g)(1) runs from the expiration of the term of probation, not from the dismissal. The two dates are usually different and the dismissal is the more visible one, so the wrong date is the obvious failure mode. The registry requires written confirmation of the probation-expiry date from the supervising probation office or the clerk, and requires the participant's own answer to be checked against it. This route computes nothing: it states the participant's two dates side by side and never asserts that the year has run.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That any waiting-period computation downstream measures from probation expiry, never from the dismissal date.

counselFlags.statement: A person as to whom dismissal and discharge have been effected is not guilty of perjury, false swearing or otherwise giving a false statement by reason of failing to disclose the arrest or trial, EXCEPT in response to an inquiry made in connection with a subsequent offence under § 17C-5-2. The exception has to travel with the protection wherever the protection is stated. Separately, the committed state pack's own never-say list forbids telling a participant that expungement destroys every record, that no one can ever see it again, or that they never have to disclose it anywhere; and the profile records that law-enforcement-type job applicants and legally required background checks may still reach expunged convictions.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That the subsequent-offence exception is carried in every participant statement of the disclosure protection.

The five official SCA-C PDFs in the committed state pack do carry sha256 values, but none of them is a form for this track.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: Record source hashes for § 17C-5-2b, § 17C-5-2, § 61-11-25 and the Court Forms index before this route leaves internal review.

profilePassageReferenced.passage: Pathway / Main authority / Best used for — Acquittal or dismissal, not in exchange for guilty plea (61-11-25); Successful pretrial diversion or deferred adjudication dismissal (61-11-25, plus 61-11-22 / 61-11-22a); Misdemeanor conviction expungement (61-11-26); Nonviolent felony conviction expungement (61-11-26); Accelerated treatment/job-readiness route (61-11-26a); First-offense controlled-substance possession conditional discharge (60A-4-407); Motor-vehicle/CDL limitation (61-11-26b) — Blocks certain traffic/CDL/DUI expungements; Full and unconditional pardon expungement (5-1-16a); Sex-trafficking [victim vacatur and expungement (61-14-9)]; [juvenile records (49-5-104)].
profilePassageReferenced.reading: This is the profile's complete enumeration of West Virginia record-clearing pathways and § 17C-5-2b is not among them. The profile's only occurrences of '17C-5-2' say that DUI under 17C-5-2 is excluded from pretrial diversion under 61-11-22, and its Motor-vehicle/CDL row records 61-11-26b as blocking certain DUI expungements. Both statements are about other statutes. The profile therefore records NO legal unit for a § 17C-5-2b deferral to omit from units[]: its silence is an absence of any deferral pathway, not an omission from this route. The whole unit structure comes from the pinned registry entry. The profile is used in this route only for the West Virginia court-level fact at sourceSections[15] ('Court: circuit, magistrate, municipal'), the SCA-C form catalogue at packetGenerator.sourceFormStatements, and the copy guardrails.

provenance.profileSilenceNote: The compiled WV profile contains no occurrence of '17C-5-2b', 'Test and Lock', '17C-5A-3a' or any DUI-deferral pathway.
